newsitem.title: UK: BP to enter Japan's retail gasoline market.
newsitem.headline: BP to enter Japan's retail gasoline market.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc on Wednesday confirmed it will enter Japan's highly competitive gasoline retail market under a deal with the owner of a Japanese supermarket chain.
As part of the deal with Iseya Kosan, BP said it would build and operate a network of filling stations next to a number of new Beisia shopping malls and do-it-yourself stores.
Earlier, a Beisia spokesman told Reuters the companies had reached a joint venture agreement.
BP's shares firmed 1.5p to 824 at 0940 GMT.
BP said it would initially build five pilot sites in the Gunma prefecture, about 100 kilometres north of central Tokyo, by the end of the first quarter of 1998.
The first site, at Beisia Super Mall Isesaki, will open at the end of this year.
If the pilot sites prove successful, the plan will be extended to other Beisia stores over the next six to seven years, creating a network of more than 100 filling stations, BP said in a statement.
The stations will be built to BP's international design and will have car washes and other conveniences.

BP's sales into Japan, where it has done business since the 1950s, account for about 3.0 percent of BP group turnover, with sales of crude oil, oil products, coal and bulk chemicals being the main activities. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
